subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should macOS Dashboard browser auth be shared-token/password-only, or may it inject native/operator device tokens into the embedded Control UI?
rationale: The two linked Dashboard auth PRs intentionally encode opposite credential-boundary policies, and changing token fallback behavior can affect existing authenticated Dashboard upgrades.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Keep native device tokens limited to native websocket clients, update this PR for every current Dashboard caller, and close or narrow the native-token parity sibling path.

options.title: Preserve native-token parity
options.body: Reject or pause this PR and continue with the sibling direction that routes Dashboard startup through native/operator token resolution.

options.title: Accept a transitional fallback
options.body: Define a temporary compatibility mode with explicit migration or recovery proof before removing native-token browser injection later.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Keep native device tokens limited to native websocket clients, update this PR for every current Dashboard caller, and close or narrow the native-token parity sibling path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored both the native Dashboard origin and the recent endpoint-change reload path that now intersects this auth decision.
